status: drafted via multi-agent workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: Read the full extracted Ethiopian-translation text for Numbers (all 36 chapters, sampled/verified extensively across chapters 1-27, 31, and 35-36 including every major narrative and legal section) directly from Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/numbers_4.json before drafting, per this project's grounding rule. Unlike this same Ethiopian Bible's Ezra (a genuinely different 9-chapter/1-Esdras-tradition text) or other deuterocanonical additions found elsewhere in this translation set, this book's Numbers is textually identical to the standard/KJV-tradition Numbers throughout every chapter checked - same 36 chapters, same narrative arc (census, camp order, Levite consecration, the spies and rebellion at Kadesh, Korah's rebellion, Aaron's death and Eleazar's succession, Balaam and Balak, Baal-peor and Phinehas's zeal, the second census, Zelophehad's daughters' inheritance petition, the Midianite war, Transjordan settlement, the wilderness journey list, and the cities of refuge/inheritance-marriage laws closing the book). No real structural or content divergence from the established KJV Numbers Character Index was found, so this draft mirrors that file's tier structure and cast (verified independently against this translation's own text at every verse cited, not copied blind) with ids re-suffixed '_ethiopian' to avoid any cross-translation id collision. One minor textual variant spotted and flagged, not silently resolved: Numbers 36:11 in this file spells the eldest daughter's name 'Mahlal' rather than the 'Mahlah' used everywhere else in the book (26:33, 27:1) - almost certainly an extraction-artifact typo rather than a deliberate translation choice, since 36:1-10 and every other appearance use 'Mahlah,' but left as an open flag rather than silently corrected, per the project's scripture-fidelity rule. As in the KJV indexing pass, Zelophehad's five daughters are one major (Mahlah, named first in both group listings) plus four submanagers rather than five separate majors, since the text never differentiates their individual actions; Eleazar is indexed as a full manager (not a submanager under Aaron) because his succession to the high priesthood on Mount Hor (20:25-28) is a book-specific pivotal event in Numbers itself, matching the KJV file's own reasoning for the same promotion.

characters.name: Moses

verses.note: 'Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth'
Intercedes for Israel after the spies' report, averting destruction
Strikes the rock at Meribah in anger instead of speaking to it as commanded — barred from entering the promised land as a result
Commissions Joshua as his successor by the laying on of hands

funFacts: The consequence of striking the rock (Numbers 20:12) is arguably the single most personally costly moment in his entire story — barred from the one goal that has driven the whole journey since Exodus 3.

characters.name: Mahlah

verses.note: With her four sisters, petitions Moses for their father's inheritance since he died with no sons — the LORD rules in their favor, setting a lasting precedent

funFacts: Named first of the five sisters every time they appear as a group in this translation's text too (27:1, 36:11) — the reason she's indexed as the major manager here, with her sisters as submanagers, rather than five separate tiers for five people who otherwise act as one unit throughout.
